title: Make the shipped frame and the docs match what OpenCode support actually delivers
action: Final judge findings on the shipped surface, all four traceable to one theme — what ships must equal what the docs claim. (1) release_manifest.rs:330-420 enumerates the shipped frame (skills/, .claude-plugin/skills/, .codex-plugin/skills/, packages/bee/**, plugin manifests, installers) but NOT .opencode/plugins/, so a release that loses bee-guard.ts stays green on release-manifest --check while installing nothing — the third belt can vanish silently; add the root to the inventory and regenerate the manifest. (2) onboard/agents.rs:112-116 renders .claude/agents/bee-*.md into a host repo but nothing renders .opencode/agent/bee-*.md, so worker dispatch (D4) works only in this checkout — render the four opencode agent definitions the same way, from the same source of truth as the hand-authored ones, and drop the now-obsolete 'a promise bee cannot keep yet' note in status_full/store.rs:934-937 if the rendering makes it keepable (reserve that file first). (3) docs/06-runtime-integration.md still teaches Node-era mechanisms that no longer exist: :107 points at source-identity.mjs (gone; the logic is onboard/source.rs:416-500), and :33/:113-128/:135/:140 describe .bee/bin/lib/*.mjs and inject.mjs as live (that tree is deleted — release_manifest.rs:342-345 says so) — correct each to the Rust reality. (4) docs/01-distillation.md:166 and docs/02-architecture.md:218,222 still teach dual-runtime as the contract and point readers at the rewritten doc — bring both to three runtimes. Where a claim would need work bee has not done, write the honest smaller claim rather than the aspiration.

truths: A release missing .opencode/plugins/bee-guard.ts fails release-manifest --check instead of passing
An onboarded host repo receives the four .opencode/agent/bee-*.md worker definitions
No doc names a deleted Node-era file or tree as a live mechanism
No surviving dual-runtime claim in docs/01, docs/02, or docs/06
